summary: HB 333 (84 Del. Laws c. 307, signed 17 Jul 2024) created the Delaware AI Commission (29 Del. C. §§ 9041C et seq.) to inventory agency generative-AI use and recommend guidelines. No private-sector duty and no PRA. Subchapter expires 17 Jul 2034 unless extended. Student member provisions are not a separate row.

short_title: Election deepfake prohibition and disclosure
enacted_date: 2025-03-25 (governor letter in Senate Journal 2025-03-31; approved SB 164)
effective_date: 2025-07-01 (South Dakota default; no delayed sentence in enrolled act)
who_regulated: Any person who disseminates a deepfake or enters into a contract/agreement to disseminate a deepfake (§ 12-26-33)
hook: Deepfake / synthetic media in elections: within 90 days of an election, no dissemination with intent to injure a candidate if the person knows or reasonably should know the item is a deepfake and it lacks the § 12-26-37 disclosure
carve_outs: Does not apply if the deepfake is satire or parody; bona fide news broadcast that acknowledges authenticity questions, or paid broadcast/publish of a deepfake; paid internet/newspaper/periodical of general circulation; 47 U.S.C. § 230 internet computer service / ISP / domain / cloud / other technical-automatic-intermediate host (§ 12-26-34)
enforcer: Attorney General (injunction); criminal prosecution (Class 1 misdemeanor). Candidate injured or likely injured, and the individual depicted, may seek injunction (§ 12-26-35)
private_suit: PRA — candidate and depicted individual may recover damages, reasonable costs and attorney fees, and other proper relief (§ 12-26-36). Injunction also available to AG, candidate, depicted individual (§ 12-26-35). No liquidated floor.
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages. Civil: damages (unquantified) + costs/fees. Crime: Class 1 misdemeanor (not a private liquidated PRA).
cure_period: none in enrolled act (disclosure is an affirmative defense, not a cure window)
plaintiffs_together: liable to the candidate and the individual depicted (§ 12-26-36); no class rule in enrolled act
fee_shifting: yes — reasonable costs and attorney fees to the civil plaintiff (§ 12-26-36)
nexus: within ninety days of an election (§ 12-26-33); chapter is offenses against the elective franchise. No extra in-state-user sentence.
retroactivity: effective 2025-07-01 — not a general retroactivity clause
safe_harbor: affirmative defense if disclosure states: 'This (image/video/audio) has been manipulated or generated by artificial intelligence' with specified size/superimpose/audio read-in requirements (§ 12-26-37). Also the § 12-26-34 exceptions.
criminal_overlay: also crime — Class 1 misdemeanor (§ 12-26-33) plus civil damages/injunction
federal_preemption: 47 U.S.C. § 230 (Jan. 3, 2024) cited for internet-computer-service exception (§ 12-26-34(4)); not a general federal-preemption clause
ai_definition: Artificial intelligence: any machine-based system that, for any explicit or implicit objective, infers from the inputs received by the system how to generate content, decisions, predictions, recommendations, or other outputs, which can influence physical or virtual environments. Deepfake: any image, audio recording, or video recording created or manipulated with the use of artificial intelligence or other digital technology that is so realistic a reasonable person would believe it depicts the speech or conduct of an actual individual who did not in fact engage in the speech or conduct (§ 12-26-32)
summary: SB 164 (SL 2025 ch. 68; governor approved 25 Mar 2025; in force 1 Jul 2025) adds SDCL §§ 12-26-32–37. Within 90 days of an election, a person may not disseminate (or contract to disseminate) a deepfake with intent to injure a candidate if the person knows or reasonably should know it is a deepfake and it lacks the specified AI-manipulation disclosure. Class 1 misdemeanor. AG, injured candidate, or depicted individual may seek an injunction. A disseminator is liable to the candidate and depicted individual for damages, reasonable costs, and attorney fees (clear-and-convincing proof of knowing use). Satire/parody, specified news/paid-media, and technical § 230 hosts are excepted. No liquidated private floor.

citation_bill: SDCL § 22-21-4 (digitally fabricated material, subd. (3)) and § 22-21-4.1 (SB 41, SL 2026, ch. 104)
short_title: Digitally fabricated intimate material — criminal invasion of privacy
effective_date: 2026-07-01 (South Dakota default; session law has no delayed sentence)
who_regulated: Any individual who, without consent or knowledge of the depicted individual and with the listed harm/self-gratify/harass intents, knowingly and intentionally creates, discloses, disseminates, distributes, or sells digitally fabricated material of an identifiable individual (§ 22-21-4(3))
hook: Intimate deepfake / digitally fabricated material: authentic-appearing image/photo/video/visual depiction adapted, generated, or modified to falsely depict appearance, conduct, or voice, showing identifiable person in nudity or sexual conduct
carve_outs: Consent or knowledge of the depicted individual defeats the offense. Subdivision (3) is creation/disclosure/distribution/sale — not possession. No ICS carve-out in SB 41 enrolled text.
enforcer: criminal prosecution
private_suit: none in SB 41 / §§ 22-21-4, 22-21-4.1 (crime only this pass)
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages. Crime: Class 5 felony for subdivision (3). Subdivisions (1)–(2) remain Class 1 misdemeanor (Class 6 felony if victim ≤17 and perpetrator ≥21, or subsequent).
nexus: silent
retroactivity: effective 2026-07-01 — not a general retroactivity clause
criminal_overlay: crime-only (Class 5 felony for digitally fabricated material)
ai_definition: Digitally fabricated material: an image, photograph, video, or other visual depiction that appears to an ordinary person to be an authentic depiction of an identifiable individual and is adapted, generated, or modified to falsely depict an individual's appearance, conduct, or voice. Identifiable: recognizable as a specific individual by face, likeness, or other distinguishing characteristics (§ 22-21-4.1). Statute does not use the words artificial intelligence.
summary: SB 41 (SL 2026 ch. 104; signed 16 Mar 2026; in force 1 Jul 2026) amends SDCL § 22-21-4 and adds § 22-21-4.1. Without the depicted individual's consent or knowledge, and with intent to self-gratify, alarm, annoy, embarrass, harass, invade privacy, threaten, or cause listed harm, a person may not knowingly and intentionally create, disclose, disseminate, distribute, or sell digitally fabricated material depicting an identifiable individual in nudity or sexual conduct. Digitally fabricated material is authentic-appearing visual content adapted, generated, or modified to falsely depict appearance, conduct, or voice. Subdivision (3) is a Class 5 felony. No PRA and no AI word in the enrolled act. Possession is not the new felony.

citation_bill: SDCL §§ 22-24A-2 (computer-generated child pornography definition), 22-24A-35 to 22-24A-42 (SB 79, SL 2024, ch. 87)
short_title: Computer-generated child pornography — possess/distribute/manufacture
effective_date: 2024-07-01 (South Dakota default; session law has no delayed sentence)
who_regulated: Any person who knowingly possesses, sells/distributes, or creates/causes/permits creation of computer-generated child pornography or a visual depiction of a minor in a prohibited sexual act (§§ 22-24A-35–37)
hook: AI / computer-generated CSAM: visual depiction of an actual minor adapted to prohibited sexual acts; actual adult adapted to appear as a minor in such acts; or an individual indistinguishable from an actual minor created by AI or other computer technology
carve_outs: Affirmative defense that the visual depiction is of the person charged and no other person appears (§ 22-24A-41). Court may depart from mandatory sentence on written mitigating findings (§ 22-24A-42). Consent of the minor/parent or mistake of age is not a defense (§ 22-24A-40). Existing civil-damages chapter 22-24A-7 applies to §§ 22-24A-1 to 22-24A-20, not to new §§ 22-24A-35–42.
enforcer: criminal prosecution
private_suit: none in SB 79 for the new possess/distribute/manufacture sections. Pre-existing § 22-24A-7 civil-damages path does not list §§ 22-24A-35–42.
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages. Crime: possess Class 4 felony (mandatory 1 year first / 5 years subsequent); distribute Class 3 felony (mandatory 5 / 10 years); manufacture Class 2 felony (mandatory 10 / 20 years).
plaintiffs_together: n/a (no PRA in SB 79 for the new sections)
nexus: silent
retroactivity: effective 2024-07-01; out-of-state convictions count as priors (§ 22-24A-38) — not a general retroactivity clause
safe_harbor: self-depiction affirmative defense (§ 22-24A-41); mitigating-circumstances sentencing departure (§ 22-24A-42)
ai_definition: Computer-generated child pornography: any visual depiction of (a) an actual minor created, adapted, or modified to depict that minor engaged in a prohibited sexual act; (b) an actual adult created, adapted, or modified to depict that adult as a minor engaged in a prohibited sexual act; or (c) an individual indistinguishable from an actual minor created by the use of artificial intelligence or other computer technology capable of processing and interpreting specific data inputs to create a visual depiction. Indistinguishable: an ordinary person would conclude the depiction is of an actual minor engaged in a prohibited sexual act (§ 22-24A-2)
summary: SB 79 (SL 2024 ch. 87; signed 12 Feb 2024; in force 1 Jul 2024) defines computer-generated child pornography in SDCL § 22-24A-2, including AI-created indistinguishable minors, and adds possess/distribute/manufacture crimes at §§ 22-24A-35–37 (Class 4 / 3 / 2 felonies with mandatory minimums). Consent and mistake of age are not defenses. No PRA in the new sections; the older § 22-24A-7 civil-damages statute was not amended to cover them.

citation_bill: Miss. Code Ann. § 97-13-47 (SB 2577, Laws 2024, ch. 467)
short_title: Wrongful dissemination of election digitizations (deepfakes)
who_regulated: A person who disseminates a digitization or enters into a contract or other agreement to disseminate a digitization (§ 97-13-47(2))
hook: Election deepfake / digitization: realistic alteration or AI/software-created image or audio (commonly called deepfakes) disseminated within 90 days of an election, without depicted-individual consent, with intent to injure a candidate, influence election results, or deter voting, with knowledge or actual knowledge it is a digitization
carve_outs: ICS as defined in 47 U.S.C. § 230(f); information/communications service as defined in 47 U.S.C. § 153; bona fide news broadcast; paid broadcast/online platform; news periodical that states the communication does not accurately represent a ballot issue or candidate; satire or parody; security/fraud/investigation receipt or dissemination (§ 97-13-47(6)). Disclaimer defense: clear and prominent language throughout that the depicted individual did not engage in the speech/conduct (§ 97-13-47(5)).
enforcer: Criminal prosecution. Injunctive cause of action by Attorney General; district attorney (if depicted individual resides in district or impact on district); depicted individual; injured/likely-injured candidate; political party whose nominee is on the ballot (§ 97-13-47(4))
private_suit: PAG — injunction/removal only for depicted individual, candidate, or political party (and AG/DA). No damages PRA in the act.
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages. Crime: up to 1 year and/or $5,000; or up to 5 years and/or $10,000 if intent to incite/cause violence, cause bodily harm, or deter voting, or prior conviction within 5 years.
cure_period: none in the act (disclaimer is a defense to prosecution, not a cure window)
nexus: dissemination within ninety days of an election; DA venue if depicted individual is a resident of the district or the digitization could/has impacted the district (§ 97-13-47(2),(4))
retroactivity: effective 2024-07-01 — not a general retroactivity clause
safe_harbor: clear-and-prominent throughout-digitization disclaimer is a defense to prosecution (§ 97-13-47(5)); subsection (6) exceptions
criminal_overlay: also crime — misdemeanor-scale (1 year/$5,000) or felony-scale (5 years/$10,000) plus injunctive PAG
federal_preemption: 47 U.S.C. §§ 230(f) and 153 cited as entity exceptions; not a general federal-preemption clause
ai_definition: Digitization: to alter an image or audio in a realistic manner utilizing an image or audio of a person other than the person depicted, computer-generated images or audio, commonly called deepfakes; also creation of image or audio through software, machine learning artificial intelligence, or any other computer-generated or technological means, including a digital representation of speech or conduct that a reasonable person would believe depicts speech/conduct of an individual who did not engage in it and that was substantially dependent on technical means rather than physical/verbal impersonation (§ 97-13-47(1)(b))
summary: SB 2577 (Laws 2024 ch. 467; signed 30 Apr 2024; in force 1 Jul 2024) creates Miss. Code § 97-13-47. Knowing dissemination of a nonconsensual election digitization (AI/deepfake image or audio) within 90 days of an election, with intent to injure a candidate, influence results, or deter voting, is a crime (1 year/$5,000, or 5 years/$10,000 with aggravators). AG, DA, depicted individual, candidate, or ballot-nominee party may seek an injunction and removal. No damages PRA. Disclaimer, satire, news, paid carriage, and § 230 ICS are defenses/exceptions.

citation_bill: Miss. Code Ann. § 97-5-31 (as amended; definitions for §§ 97-5-33 through 97-5-37) (HB 1126 § 9, Laws 2024, ch. 456)
short_title: Morphed / computer-generated images of identifiable minors — child-exploitation definitions
who_regulated: Persons subject to child-exploitation crimes in §§ 97-5-33 through 97-5-37, via the amended definitions (producing includes morphing; visual depiction includes morphed computer reproductions)
hook: AI-adjacent CSAM: morphed image is a computer or computer-generated visual depiction created, adapted, or modified so an identifiable minor appears to engage in sexual conduct or sexually explicit nudity; sexually explicit conduct includes actual, morphed, or simulated acts
carve_outs: Identifiable-child paragraph shall not be construed to require proof of the actual identity of the identifiable child (§ 97-5-31(h)). Definitions require an identifiable child (minor at creation/adaptation, or whose childhood image was used) — purely synthetic unmatched-to-a-real-child imagery is outside this definitional amendment. Walker Montgomery digital-service sections 1–7 of the same act are generic online-minors duties (no AI/ADS hook) and are not this row.
enforcer: criminal prosecution under §§ 97-5-33 through 97-5-37 (penalties in those sections; dollar/year table not pulled this pass)
private_suit: none in HB 1126 § 9 for the definitional CSAM amendment. (Walker Montgomery DSP duties are AG UDAP via 75-24-5(q) — skipped as generic privacy.)
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages in § 9. Crime: child-exploitation felonies in §§ 97-5-33 et seq. (penalty numbers unconfirmed this pass).
plaintiffs_together: n/a (no PRA in the CSAM definitional amendment)
nexus: silent
retroactivity: effective 2024-07-01 — not a general retroactivity clause
criminal_overlay: crime-only (definitional input to existing child-exploitation offenses)
federal_preemption: computer defined by cross-cite to 18 U.S.C. § 1030 — definitional, not a preemption clause
ai_definition: Morphed image: any visual depiction or representation, including any photograph, film, video, picture, or computer or computer-generated image or picture, whether made or produced by electronic, mechanical, simulated or other means, of sexually explicit conduct, where such visual depiction or representation has been created, adapted, or modified to appear an identifiable minor is engaging in sexual conduct or sexually explicit activity [or] appearing in a state of sexually explicit nudity (§ 97-5-31(f)). Visual depiction includes unaltered, altered or morphed reproductions by computer and technology. Statute does not use the words artificial intelligence in § 9.
summary: HB 1126 (Laws 2024 ch. 456; signed 30 Apr 2024; in force 1 Jul 2024) § 9 amends Miss. Code § 97-5-31 so child-exploitation crimes in §§ 97-5-33–37 reach morphed and computer-generated sexual images of an identifiable minor. Producing includes morphing. No AI word and no PRA in § 9. The same bill’s Walker Montgomery digital-service age/collection duties are generic kids-online (AG UDAP) and are not indexed. Penalty years/fines in § 97-5-33 were not pulled this pass.

citation_bill: W. Va. Code § 61-8-28a (SB 198, Acts 2025, ch. 80)
short_title: Nonconsensual disclosure of fabricated intimate images
who_regulated: No person may knowingly and intentionally disclose, cause to be disclosed, or threaten to disclose, with intent to harass, intimidate, threaten, humiliate, embarrass, or coerce, a fabricated intimate image of another (or a captured intimate image) (§ 61-8-28a(b))
hook: Intimate deepfake: fabricated intimate image of an identifiable depicted individual created by AI or other computer technology, depicting computer-generated intimate parts or another person’s intimate parts as the depicted individual’s
carve_outs: Does not apply to images disclosed with prior written consent of the person depicted; voluntary public/commercial exposure; disclosures through reporting illegal conduct or lawful LE/legal/medical practice (§ 61-8-28a(d)). No liability on interactive computer service (47 U.S.C. § 230(f)(2)), information service (§ 153(24)), or telecommunications service (§ 153(53)) for content provided by another (§ 61-8-28a(e)).
enforcer: criminal prosecution
private_suit: none in § 61-8-28a as amended (crime only)
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages. Crime: misdemeanor jail ≤1 year and/or fine $1,000–$5,000; second/subsequent felony imprisonment ≤3 years and/or fine $2,500–$10,000.
nexus: silent
retroactivity: effective 2025-07-09 — not a general retroactivity clause
safe_harbor: written-consent, public-exposure, and reporting/LE exceptions; ICS § 230 non-liability for others’ content
federal_preemption: 47 U.S.C. §§ 230(f)(2), 153(24), 153(53) cited as provider non-liability; not a general federal-preemption clause
ai_definition: Fabricated intimate image: an image of an identifiable depicted individual that was created by the use of artificial intelligence or other computer technology capable of processing and interpreting specific data inputs and depicts computer-generated intimate parts or the intimate parts of another human being as the intimate parts of the depicted individual (§ 61-8-28a(a)(5))
summary: SB 198 (Acts 2025 ch. 80; signed 24 Apr 2025; in force 9 Jul 2025) amends W. Va. Code § 61-8-28a so nonconsensual disclosure (or threat of disclosure) of a fabricated intimate image — AI-created intimate parts on an identifiable person — is the same crime as disclosure of a captured intimate image, with harass/intimidate intent. First offense misdemeanor (jail ≤1 year; fine $1,000–$5,000); subsequent felony (≤3 years; $2,500–$10,000). Written consent, public exposure, reporting, and § 230 ICS are excepted. No PRA in the section.

citation_bill: W. Va. Code §§ 61-8C-1 to 61-8C-3c (computer-generated child pornography; SB 198, Acts 2025, ch. 80)
short_title: Computer-generated child pornography — possess/distribute/exhibit and related offenses
who_regulated: Any person who knowingly sends, distributes, exhibits, possesses, electronically accesses with intent to view, displays, or transports a visual portrayal of a minor in sexually explicit conduct or computer-generated child pornography (§ 61-8C-3); also creation/use of a minor to create a visual portrayal (§ 61-8C-2); juveniles via delinquency (§ 61-8C-3b)
hook: AI / computer-generated CSAM: visual portrayal of an identifiable minor created/adapted/modified to depict the minor in sexually explicit conduct, or a portrayal that appears to depict a minor in such conduct if created by AI/computer technology and indistinguishable from a minor. Visual portrayal includes media created, generated, or produced in whole or in part by manipulation including artificial intelligence.
carve_outs: Drawings, cartoons, sculptures, or paintings are outside 'indistinguishable' (§ 61-8C-1(a)(8)). Article not construed to include a visual portrayal of an actual identifiable person who was not a minor when created (§ 61-8C-1(b)). Person excludes ICS/information/telecom providers for content provided by another (§ 61-8C-1(a)(4)). Official-duty possession/distribution by LE, prosecutors, defense counsel, judges, jurors, support staff, and court-order recipients is not an offense (§ 61-8C-3c(b)). Employment-scope viewers who immediately report to LE or NCMEC CyberTipline have an affirmative defense except willful/wanton misconduct (§ 61-8C-3c(d)).
enforcer: criminal prosecution; juvenile delinquency for minors under § 61-8C-3b
private_suit: none in the enrolled CSAM article amendments (crime only)
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages. Crime (distribute/possess/exhibit CG CSAM): 50 or fewer images — 2–5 years and/or ≤$5,000; >50 and <300 — 3–15 years and/or ≤$10,000; 300+ images or violence/bestiality — 5–20 years and/or ≤$25,000. Video ≤5 minutes counts as 100 images.
nexus: silent
thresholds: image-count penalty tiers (50 / 300); video duration conversion
retroactivity: effective 2025-07-09; not-a-defense that the depicted person later turned 18 or is deceased — not a general retroactivity clause
safe_harbor: ICS definitional exclusion; official-duty exemption; mandatory-reporting affirmative defense; indistinguishable excludes drawings/cartoons/sculptures/paintings
criminal_overlay: crime-only (felonies; juvenile delinquency overlay for minors)
federal_preemption: 47 U.S.C. §§ 230(f)(2), 153(24), 153(53) in the 'person' definition; not a general federal-preemption clause
ai_definition: Computer-generated child pornography: (A) any visual portrayal of an identifiable minor created, adapted, or modified to depict the minor engaging in sexually explicit conduct; or (B) any visual portrayal that appears to depict a minor engaged in sexually explicit conduct if created by AI or other computer technology capable of processing and interpreting specific data inputs and indistinguishable from a minor. Indistinguishable: an ordinary person would conclude the portrayal is of an actual minor engaged in sexually explicit conduct. Identifiable minor: a portrayal that depicts a minor identifiable from the matter or connected information, created or altered by AI or similar computer technology (§ 61-8C-1)
record_retention: prohibited media shall not be published to the public; Supreme Court of Appeals requested to promulgate access/handling rules (§ 61-8C-3c) — not a business retention period
summary: The same SB 198 (in force 9 Jul 2025) rewrites W. Va. Code art. 61-8C to cover computer-generated child pornography, including purely synthetic indistinguishable minors created by AI and morphed identifiable minors. Knowingly distributing, possessing, exhibiting, or accessing with intent to view is a felony with image-count tiers (2–5 / 3–15 / 5–20 years). ICS providers for others’ content, official-duty handlers, and prompt NCMEC/LE reporters (except willful/wanton) are excepted. No PRA. Drawings/cartoons/paintings are outside indistinguishable.

citation_bill: La. R.S. 14:73.13 (SB 175, Acts 2023, No. 457, as amended by HB 119, Acts 2026, No. 782 / Ivy Daniels Act)
short_title: Unlawful deepfakes
enacted_date: 2023 (Act 457); 2026 Act 782 (governor calendar day unconfirmed in enrolled PDFs)
effective_date: 2023-08-01 (Act 457 digest); Act 782 no stated date — Louisiana default 2026-08-01
who_regulated: Any person who knowingly creates/possesses a deepfake depicting a minor in sexual conduct, or who advertises/distributes/exhibits/exchanges/promotes/sells sexual material that is a nonconsensual deepfake of another person
hook: Deepfake / synthetic sexual media (minors: create or possess; adults: distribute sexual deepfake without consent)
carve_outs: Deepfake excludes political/public-interest/newsworthy works including commentary, criticism, satire, or parody, or material with content/context/clear disclosure visible throughout that a reasonable person would understand is not a real event (73.13(C)(1))
enforcer: criminal prosecution
private_suit: none in 73.13 (crime only)
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages. Criminal fines: create/possess minor deepfake <= $10,000; distribute adult or minor sexual deepfake <= $50,000
nexus: venue silent in original act beyond general criminal venue
retroactivity: Act 457 effective 2023-08-01; Act 782 educator/student add-ons treated as 2026-08-01 default — not a general retroactivity clause
safe_harbor: disclosure / satire-parody / newsworthy exclusion in the deepfake definition
criminal_overlay: also crime — hard labor 5-20 years (create/possess minor) with 5 years without PPS; distribute 10-30 years (10 years without PPS if minor). Act 782: extra 2 years consecutive if educator and victim is a student
ai_definition: Deepfake: audio or visual media in electronic format created, altered, or digitally manipulated so it would falsely appear to a reasonable observer to be an authentic record of actual speech or conduct, or to replace an individual's likeness with another (73.13(C)(1))
summary: Act 457 (2023) created R.S. 14:73.13. Knowing creation or possession of a sexual deepfake of a minor is 5-20 years hard labor (5 without PPS) and/or <=$10,000. Knowing distribution of a nonconsensual sexual deepfake of another person is 10-30 years and/or <=$50,000 (10 years without PPS if a minor). Political/newsworthy/satire and on-screen disclosure are excluded from the definition. HB 119 / Act 782 added educator-student consecutive time. Crime only; no PRA in the section.

citation_bill: La. R.S. 14:73.14 and 14:73.14.1 (SB 6, Acts 2024, No. 142, as amended/added by HB 119, Acts 2026, No. 782 / Ivy Daniels Act)
short_title: Unlawful dissemination, sale, or (minors) possession of AI-created nude images
enacted_date: 2024-05-22 (SB 6 signed — Act 142); 2026 Act 782 (governor calendar day unconfirmed in enrolled PDF)
effective_date: 2024-08-01 (Act 142); Act 782 no stated date — Louisiana default 2026-08-01 for 73.14.1 and penalty upgrades
who_regulated: Any person who, with intent to coerce/harass/intimidate, disseminates or sells an AI-created nude/undress image of a recognizable actual person without license/authorization; any person who possesses such an AI image of a person under 17
hook: AI-created intimate images (adult dissemination/sale; minor possession)
carve_outs: ICS / email provider / telecommunications or information service (47 U.S.C. 153) / access-software provider used by another to commit the act. Possession crime: person who lacked specific intent to receive and did not consent to receipt. Offenders under 14: Children's Code Title VII only
enforcer: criminal prosecution; 73.14(F) does not preclude a civil action under any other applicable law (no new PRA created)
private_suit: none created in 73.14/73.14.1; 73.14(F) preserves other-law civil actions
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages. After Act 782: disseminate/sell <=1 year and/or <=$1,000; if depicted person under 17, <=5 years (1 year without PPS); possess AI nude image of person under 17: <=5 years (1 year without PPS); educator-student extra 2 years consecutive
nexus: 73.14(E): also prosecutable in the parish where the unlawful act occurred or where any video/still image was created, produced, reproduced, found, stored, received, or possessed
retroactivity: Act 142 2024-08-01; Act 782 possession crime and penalty upgrades treated as 2026-08-01 default
ai_definition: Artificial intelligence: an artificial system developed in computer software, physical hardware, or other context that solves tasks requiring human-like perception, cognition, planning, learning, communication, or physical action (73.14(C)(2); 73.14.1(B)(2)). Another person includes a person whose image was used in creating/adapting/modifying with intent to depict an actual recognizable person
summary: Act 142 (effective 1 Aug 2024) created R.S. 14:73.14: intent-to-harass dissemination or sale of an AI-created nude/undress image of a recognizable person. Act 782 (Ivy Daniels Act) raised adult penalties to <=1 year/<=$1,000, added <=5 years when the depicted person is under 17, and added 73.14.1 possession of such AI images of persons under 17 (<=5 years). ICS/telecom carve-out. No new PRA; 73.14(F) does not preclude other-law civil suits. School-notice duties in R.S. 17:416.20.1 are not a separate row.

citation_bill: La. R.S. 51:1780.1-1780.5 (SB 386, Acts 2026, No. 502) — Louisiana Data Privacy Act

private_suit: none — LUTPA private rights expressly excluded (51:1780.5(C))

insurance_situs: n/a — profiling legal-effect category includes insurance, but GLBA entity/data carve-out; not an insurance-code UR statute

summary: Act 502 (SB 386) creates the Louisiana Data Privacy Act, R.S. 51:1780.1-.5, effective 1 Jan 2027. Consumers may opt out of solely automated profiling that produces legal or similarly significant effects, including provision/denial of insurance. AG-only LUTPA enforcement with private 51:1409/1409.1 rights excluded. Time-limited 30-day AG cure 1 Jan-31 Jul 2027. GLBA FI carve-out. Not an insurance-code UR statute. citation_bill: KRS 42.722, 42.726, and a new section of KRS 42.720-42.742 (SB 4, 2025 Ky. Acts ch. 66, sections 1-3)

operative_date: 2025-03-24; COT administrative regulations to implement by 2025-12-01; first inventory report 2025-12-01
who_regulated: State departments, agencies, and administrative bodies that use/access the Commonwealth IT; COT; Artificial Intelligence Governance Committee. Developer/deployer as defined are state bodies
hook: Government use of generative AI and high-risk AI (consequential decisions); public disclaimer; human review; registry
carve_outs: COT IT-infrastructure carve-outs in 42.726(2)(f) (statewide elected officials, public postsecondary, etc.) are preexisting COT scope, not a private-sector exemption. Sections 1-3 shall not require disclosure of trade secrets, confidential/proprietary design/use information, or information that would create a security risk
enforcer: Commonwealth Office of Technology / AI Governance Committee (policy, registry, approval). No private-sector enforcer in sections 1-3
private_suit: none in sections 1-3
statutory_damages: none
nexus: state departments/agencies/administrative bodies using Commonwealth IT/technology infrastructure
retroactivity: emergency on signature — not a general retroactivity clause
ai_definition: AI: use of machine learning and related technologies that uses data to train statistical models to perform tasks normally associated with human intelligence or perception (42.722). High-risk AI system: substantial factor in, or specifically intended to autonomously make, a consequential decision (material legal or similarly significant effect on provision/denial of services, cost, or terms). Generative AI: capable of producing synthetic audio/images/text/video
impact_assessment_discoverable: risk-management policy for high-risk systems (ISO/IEC 42001 or equivalent); annual LRC report includes registry and approve/deny rationales — public-report path, not a private discovery clause
record_retention: COT shall secure all data and implement a timeframe for data retention (SB 4 section 3(3)(c)) — no year count
summary: 2025 Ky. Acts ch. 66 sections 1-3 (emergency 24 Mar 2025) put COT policy standards and an AI Governance Committee over state-body generative and high-risk AI: registry, approval, human review of outcomes, public disclaimers when AI is used to render or inform decisions about citizens/businesses, appeal of consequential AI decisions, and ISO/IEC 42001-style risk management. No private-sector duty and no PRA. Election synthetic-media section of the same Act is a separate row.

citation_bill: KRS 117.322 (SB 4, 2025 Ky. Acts ch. 66, section 5; as later amended 2026 Ky. Acts ch. 161, section 106)
short_title: Synthetic media in electioneering communications — candidate injunctive PRA
status: in force (emergency 2025-03-24; compiled statute lists 2026-07-15 amendment effective)
who_regulated: Sponsor of an electioneering communication containing synthetic media of a candidate; medium and ad-sales representative only in the limited cases in 117.322(5)
hook: Election synthetic media (GAN-manipulated audio/video of an identifiable natural individual)
carve_outs: News/editorial/membership/business-regular-course exclusions in the electioneering-communication definition (117.001). Medium and ad-sales rep not liable except intentional disclaimer removal or changing content into synthetic media. ICS: not treated as publisher/speaker of another's content; 47 U.S.C. 230 exemption restated. Federally licensed broadcast 47 U.S.C. 315 exception in (5)
enforcer: Candidate plaintiff in Circuit Court of the county of residence; court-order noncompliance imports KRS 121.990(3) (via 121.190(1))
private_suit: PRA — candidate whose appearance/action/speech is altered may seek injunctive or other equitable relief requiring a clear conspicuous disclosure. Does not limit other available remedies (117.322(1)(b))
statutory_damages: none as a liquidated floor. Equitable disclosure order; prevailing-party fees. Failure to obey the order: KRS 121.990(3) penalties (not isolated this pass)
cure_period: none as a statutory cure; affirmative defense if the communication already includes the required disclosure (117.322(4))
fee_shifting: yes — court may award a prevailing party reasonable attorney's fees and costs (117.322(1)(b))
notice_cure: affirmative defense of existing disclosure; not a cure period
nexus: electioneering communication distributed to an audience that includes members of the relevant electorate within 45 days of a primary or regular election (117.001 definition); plaintiff files in county of residence
choice_of_law_forum: Circuit Court of the county in which the plaintiff resides (117.322(2)(a)1)
safe_harbor: clear conspicuous disclosure (definitional exclusion and affirmative defense); news/ICS/broadcast limits
criminal_overlay: civil PRA; noncompliance with the court's disclosure order is subject to KRS 121.990(3)
ai_definition: Synthetic media: audio or video of an identifiable natural individual's appearance, action, or speech intentionally manipulated with generative adversarial network techniques to create a realistic but false recording of something that did not occur, producing a fundamentally different understanding than the unaltered original (117.001). GAN and neural-network terms defined there
summary: Ch. 66 section 5 (emergency 24 Mar 2025) created KRS 117.322. A candidate whose appearance, action, or speech is altered by GAN synthetic media in an electioneering communication (generally within 45 days of a primary/regular election) may sue the sponsor in home-county Circuit Court for an injunction requiring a conspicuous disclosure, on clear-and-convincing proof. Prevailing-party fees. Disclosure is an affirmative defense. Media generally not liable except disclaimer stripping or content alteration. No liquidated damages. Compiled history notes a 15 Jul 2026 amendment (ch. 161 section 106).

citation_bill: KRS 531.300-.370 as amended (HB 207, 2024 RS)
short_title: Computer-generated image of a minor — CSAM / sexual-performance statutes
enacted_date: 2024-03 (enrolled PDF timestamp 2024-03-27; chapter number unconfirmed this pass)
effective_date: Kentucky default (no effective-date section in the unofficial enrolled PDF) — treated as 2024-07-15 unless a delayed sentence exists in the Acts volume (unconfirmed)
who_regulated: Persons who use, possess, distribute, advertise, or promote matter portraying a sexual performance by a minor or a computer-generated image of a minor (KRS ch. 531 as amended)
hook: CSAM / sexual performance — computer-generated image of a minor (identifiable person; actual minor need not exist)
carve_outs: silent in the extracted CGI definitional/proof sections this pass (preexisting ch. 531 exceptions not re-pulled)
enforcer: criminal prosecution
private_suit: none in HB 207
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages
nexus: silent
retroactivity: treated as 2024 default — not a general retroactivity clause
criminal_overlay: also crime (Class B/C/D felonies depending on the amended 531 offense)
ai_definition: Computer-generated image: any visual depiction (photograph, film, video, or picture) created, adapted, or modified by a computer to appear to be an identifiable person. Identifiable person: recognizable by face, likeness, or other distinguishing characteristic. New section: Commonwealth need not prove actual identity or age of the minor, or that the minor actually exists, in a ch. 531 prosecution involving a CGI of a minor. Statute does not say artificial intelligence
summary: HB 207 (2024 RS) amends KRS Chapter 531 so matter includes a computer-generated image and defines CGI as a depiction created/adapted/modified by a computer to appear to be an identifiable person. Sexual-performance, distribution, and advertising offenses reach CGI of a minor. A new section provides the Commonwealth need not prove the minor's actual identity, age, or existence. Crime only. Chapter number, governor day, and default effective calendar day unconfirmed in the unofficial enrolled PDF. Adult NCII statute KRS 531.120 does not say AI — not a row.

short_title: Unauthorized disclosure of intimate images (digitally forged)
who_regulated: A person who intentionally disseminates an intimate image or a digitally forged intimate image of another without effective consent
hook: Digitally forged intimate image (machine-learning / computer-generated) plus authentic intimate images
carve_outs: Law-enforcement-created images pursuant to an otherwise lawful criminal investigation (16-15-332(F))
enforcer: criminal prosecution
private_suit: none in Act 37
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages. Criminal fines: harm/profit first offense <= $5,000 (felony <=5 years); subsequent <= $10,000 and 1-10 years (min unsuspendable). Without harm/profit intent: first misdemeanor <= $5,000 / <=1 year; subsequent felony <= $5,000 / <=5 years
nexus: silent
thresholds: none. Multiple images of the same individual as part of a common act = a single offense
retroactivity: effective on signature — not a general retroactivity clause
ai_definition: Digitally forged intimate image: intimate image of an identifiable individual that appears to a reasonable person indistinguishable from an authentic visual depiction, generated or substantially modified using machine-learning techniques or any other computer-generated or machine-generated means to falsely depict appearance or conduct, even if labeled inauthentic (16-15-330(1))
record_retention: images cannot be duplicated for criminal discovery requests and motions (16-15-332(D)) — not a retention-year rule
summary: 2025 Act No. 37 (H. 3058), signed 12 May 2025, adds sections 16-15-330 and 16-15-332. Intentional dissemination of an intimate image or a digitally forged (ML/computer-generated) intimate image without effective consent is a crime, with felony penalties if done with intent to harm or for profit. Creation consent is not dissemination consent. Crime only; no PRA. No SC election-deepfake statute (H. 3517 failed). No insurance-code AI UR statute found.

citation_bill: S.C. Code section 16-15-390 (S. 28, 2025 Act No. 57)
short_title: Obscene visual representations of child sexual abuse (computer-generated; minor need not exist)
who_regulated: Any person who knowingly produces, distributes, solicits, or possesses with intent to distribute — or possesses — an obscene visual depiction or representation that depicts a minor in sexually explicit conduct/activity/nudity
hook: CSAM — computer-generated image or picture; depicted minor need not actually exist
carve_outs: Specified LE/prosecutor/DOC employees acting in official capacity; telecommunications or information service provider (47 U.S.C. 153) for content provided by another. Arrest warrant only after state grand-jury true bill or ICAC+AG probable-cause finding
enforcer: criminal prosecution (warrant path limited as above)
private_suit: none in Act 57
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages. Felony imprisonment no more than 10 years (produce/distribute/solicit/possess-with-intent and simple possession). Minor first-offender: family-court misdemeanor
nexus: silent
retroactivity: effective on approval — not a general retroactivity clause
safe_harbor: LE official-capacity; telecom/information-service for third-party content
criminal_overlay: also crime; sex-offender-registry add in the Act
ai_definition: Visual depiction or representation includes any computer image or picture or computer-generated image or picture, whether made or produced by electronic, mechanical, or other means (16-15-390(A)(2)). It is not a required element that the minor depicted actually exists (16-15-390(E)). Statute does not say artificial intelligence
summary: 2025 Act No. 57 (S. 28), effective 22 May 2025, adds section 16-15-390. Producing, distributing, soliciting, possessing with intent, or possessing an obscene visual depiction of a minor in sexually explicit conduct is a felony (<=10 years). Computer-generated pictures are in the definition; the depicted minor need not exist. Crime only. Companion morphed-identifiable-minor amendments are a separate row (Act 58).

short_title: Sexual exploitation of a minor — morphed images of identifiable minors
who_regulated: Persons who record/produce/distribute/possess material containing a visual representation of a minor or a morphed image of an identifiable minor engaged in sexual activity, as amended into first/second/third degree exploitation
hook: CSAM — morphed / computer-generated image of an identifiable minor
carve_outs: Family-court misdemeanor path for a minor's first morphed-image offense (degree-specific). Warrant procedures in new 16-15-412
enforcer: criminal prosecution
private_suit: none in Act 58
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages (underlying 16-15-395/-405/-410 penalties not re-isolated this pass beyond the morphed-image add)
nexus: silent
retroactivity: effective on approval — not a general retroactivity clause
ai_definition: Morphed image: any visual depiction or representation, including any photograph, film, video, picture, or computer or computer-generated image or picture, whether made or produced by electronic, mechanical, or other means (16-15-375 as amended). Identifiable minor defined in the same section
summary: 2025 Act No. 58 (S. 29), effective 22 May 2025, defines morphed image and identifiable minor in 16-15-375 and folds morphed images of identifiable minors into first, second, and third degree sexual exploitation of a minor (16-15-395, -405, -410), with a new warrant section 16-15-412. Crime only. No PRA.

citation_bill: Ala. Code 17-5-16.1 (compiled cite unconfirmed in enrolled bill) (HB 172, Act 2024-349 per fiscal/code sources)
short_title: Materially deceptive AI election media
enacted_date: 2024-05 (Senate passed 2024-05-08; House concurred 2024-05-09; governor calendar day unconfirmed in enrolled PDF)
who_regulated: A person who distributes, or agrees to distribute, materially deceptive media (AI-produced image/audio/video falsely depicting speech or conduct) within 90 days before an election with the specified knowledge and dual intents
hook: Election deepfake / materially deceptive AI media
carve_outs: Disclaimer safe harbor (manipulated-by-technical-means plus speech/conduct did not occur; video throughout / audio bookends / image visible; citation to original if edited). Satire/parody substantially dependent on physical/verbal impersonation not technology/AI. Bona fide newscast with authenticity acknowledgment. Distributors without actual knowledge and without intent (ICS/broadcast/periodical/streaming). 47 U.S.C. ch. 5 / FCC political-programming and section 230 constructions. Creator definition excludes mere distributors/developers of AI tech
enforcer: Criminal prosecution; permanent injunction: AG, depicted individual, injured/likely-injured candidate, or entity representing interests of voters likely to be deceived
private_suit: PAG/limited PRA — permanent injunction only (clear and convincing that defendant knew the media falsely represented the depicted individual). No damages PRA in enrolled act. Non-AG plaintiff awarded injunction: court may award costs and attorney fees
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages. Crime: Class A misdemeanor; second or subsequent conviction within five years is a Class D felony
cure_period: none as a cure period; disclaimer is an element-out / safe harbor
fee_shifting: yes — if a non-AG plaintiff is awarded permanent injunctive relief, the court may award costs and attorney fees to the plaintiff; frivolous complaint: court may award costs/fees to defendant
notice_cure: disclaimer safe harbor (not a cure period)
nexus: distribution within 90 days before a federal/state/legislative/judicial/countywide/local/general/primary/runoff/special election
retroactivity: operative 2024-10-01 — not a general retroactivity clause
safe_harbor: specified disclaimer; satire/parody impersonation; bona fide news with authenticity acknowledgment; no-actual-knowledge distributor list
criminal_overlay: also crime (Class A misdemeanor / Class D felony repeat within 5 years)
federal_preemption: shall not alter rights/obligations/immunities under 47 U.S.C. ch. 5, FCC political-programming rules, other federal law, or 47 U.S.C. 230
ai_definition: Artificial intelligence: any artificial system or generative AI system that performs tasks under varying and unpredictable circumstances without significant human oversight or that can learn from experience and improve performance when exposed to data sets. Materially deceptive media: image/audio/video that falsely depicts speech/conduct, that a reasonable viewer/listener would incorrectly believe, and that was produced by AI
summary: HB 172 (effective 1 Oct 2024) makes it a Class A misdemeanor (Class D felony on a second conviction within 5 years) to distribute AI-produced materially deceptive media within 90 days of an election, knowing it is false, intending to harm a candidate's reputation/electoral prospects, and intending to change voting patterns by deceit. Specified disclaimer is a safe harbor. AG, depicted person, injured candidate, or voter-interest entity may seek a permanent injunction on clear-and-convincing knowledge; non-AG injunction winner may get fees. No damages PRA. Compiled 17-5-16.1 / Act 2024-349 number not on the enrolled PDF.

citation_bill: 2026 Ala. SB 63 (enrolled; Act number unconfirmed in enrolled PDF) — health-benefit-plan AI utilization review
short_title: Health benefit plan AI in medical-necessity prior authorization
enacted_date: 2026-04 (House amended/passed 2026-04-08; Senate concurred 2026-04-08; governor calendar day unconfirmed in enrolled PDF; secondary trackers: 2026-04-17)
who_regulated: Health benefit plan providers (issuers, HMOs, nonprofit health-care service plans, nonprofit agricultural health-benefit organizations) and internal or contracted utilization-review units that use AI to make medical-necessity determinations on PA requests
hook: Insurance-code AI: PA medical-necessity determinations; AI may not be the sole decider of deny/delay/modify; licensed clinician must decide
carve_outs: Health benefit plan excludes accident-only, specified disease, individual hospital indemnity, credit, dental-only, Medicare supplement, LTC, disability income, other limited-benefit, liability-supplement, workers comp, auto med-pay
enforcer: Alabama Department of Insurance: notice, 30-day response, Title 27 ch. 2 art. 1 hearing; corrective plan; repeat pattern/practice: administrative fine <= $5,000 and/or suspend/revoke certificate of authority
private_suit: none in enrolled act
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages. DOI administrative fine <= $5,000 for a repeat violation occurring with such frequency as to indicate a general business pattern or practice (to State General Fund). Provider reimburses DOI investigation expenses
cure_period: 30 days to respond to DOI notice of alleged violation (enrolled (d)(1)) — not a consumer cure
nexus: plan, policy, or contract issued, delivered, or renewed in this state (health benefit plan definition)
insurance_situs: yes — Alabama insurance / health-benefit-plan UR; issued, delivered, or renewed in this state
retroactivity: effective 2026-10-01 — not a general retroactivity clause
safe_harbor: AI may be used if determinations are based on the enrollee medical history, unique clinical circumstances, and additional clinical information in the record, and a licensed physician or other competent health professional always makes any deny/delay/modify medical-necessity determination. Annual certification. Attestation by authorized representative based on reasonable reliance on internal policies/procedures and third-party vendors satisfies (b) and (c)
federal_preemption: HIPAA purpose-limitation for patient data used by the AI (enrolled (c)(3))
ai_definition: Artificial intelligence: a machine-based system that may include software or physical hardware that performs tasks, based upon data-set inputs, which require human-like perception, cognition, planning, learning, communication, or physical action and which is capable of improving performance based upon learned experience without significant human oversight toward influencing real or virtual environments
impact_assessment_discoverable: periodic review of AI use and outcomes for accuracy/reliability (enrolled (c)(2)) — not a public IA
record_retention: patient data used in UR by AI not used beyond intended/stated purpose consistent with HIPAA — no year count
summary: Enrolled SB 63 (effective 1 Oct 2026) limits AI in health-benefit-plan medical-necessity PA. AI-using providers must base determinations on the enrollee history and unique clinical circumstances, annually certify the AI does not rely on a group dataset and is fairly/equitably applied, disclose AI use in UR policies, and have a licensed clinician make every deny/delay/modify medical-necessity call. DOI enforcement; repeat pattern/practice fine <=$5,000 and/or COA suspension/revocation. No PRA. Delayed as of 2 Sep 2026.

citation_bill: Alabama Personal Data Protection Act (HB 351, 2026 RS; Act number unconfirmed in enrolled PDF)
short_title: APDPA — profiling opt-out
enacted_date: 2026-04-17 (secondary chaptered-signing reports; enrolled PDF has House origin 2026-02-24 and later concurrence — governor calendar day unconfirmed on PDF)
who_regulated: Persons that conduct business in this state or produce products/services targeted to residents and meet a threshold (controllers/processors)
hook: ADS / solely automated profiling in furtherance of significant decisions (provision/denial of credit/lending, housing, insurance, education, criminal justice, etc.)
carve_outs: Political subdivisions/boards; higher ed; national securities association (15 U.S.C. 78o-3); FI/affiliate under 15 U.S.C. ch. 94; GLBA Title V FI/affiliate or GLBA-processed data; plus listed data-type exemptions (PHI, FCRA, etc.)
enforcer: Attorney General may enforce (enrolled section 11)
private_suit: none in enrolled act (AG enforcement section only; no PRA sentence)
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages. Court may assess a civil penalty <= $15,000 per violation after failed 45-day correction (AG action)
cure_period: 45 days after AG notice of violation; correction plus express written statement that no further violations will occur bars the action (section 11(b))
nexus: conduct business in this state or produce products or services targeted to residents of this state
out_of_state_actor: produce products or services targeted to residents of this state
insurance_situs: n/a — significant-decision category includes insurance; GLBA FI carve-out; not an insurance-code UR statute
thresholds: >25,000 consumers (excluding payment-transaction-only data) OR derive >25% of gross revenue from the sale of personal data regardless of consumer count
retroactivity: effective 2027-05-01 — not a general retroactivity clause. Enrolled act has no data-protection-assessment section
ai_definition: Profiling: any form of solely-automated processing performed on personal data to evaluate, analyze, or predict personal aspects related to an identified or identifiable individual's economic situation, health, personal preferences, interests, reliability, behavior, location, or movements (enrolled definitions). Not a GenAI definition
impact_assessment_discoverable: silent (no assessment duty found in enrolled act)
summary: HB 351 (effective 1 May 2027) is the Alabama Personal Data Protection Act. Opt-out of profiling in furtherance of solely automated significant decisions, including insurance. Applies to in-state or resident-targeted businesses over 25,000 consumers or >25% revenue from sale of personal data. AG-only in the enrolled enforcement section; 45-day cure then injunction and <=$15,000/violation. GLBA carve-out. No IA duty found. Not an insurance-code UR statute. 2026 SB 129 GenAI-disclosure bill remained in committee — not law.

citation_bill: 21 O.S. 1040.13b (HB 1364, 2025; signed 2025-05-05 per session timeline)
short_title: Nonconsensual dissemination of artificially generated sexual depictions
who_regulated: A person who disseminates an artificially generated sexual depiction of another with intent or reckless disregard to harass/annoy/threaten/alarm or cause physical, emotional, reputational, or economic harm, without effective consent; plus preexisting nonconsensual private-sexual-image dissemination
hook: AI / technically generated sexual depiction of an identifiable person (intimate deepfake)
carve_outs: Criminal investigation; reporting unlawful conduct; voluntary public/commercial exposure; lawful purpose. No liability solely for third-party content on an ICS (47 U.S.C. 230(f)(2)), wireless provider, or telecommunications/broadband provider
enforcer: criminal prosecution; court may order defendant to remove the image if in the defendant's power
private_suit: none in HB 1364
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages. Misdemeanor: county jail <=1 year and/or fine <= $1,000. Financial-gain/attempted-gain: felony <=5 years (<=10 years plus sex-offender registration on second). Three or more images/depictions in six months: felony <=10 years
nexus: silent
thresholds: three or more images/depictions within six months elevates to the 10-year felony
retroactivity: effective 2025-11-01 — not a general retroactivity clause
safe_harbor: ICS/wireless/telecom for third-party content; listed lawful-purpose exceptions
ai_definition: Artificial intelligence: machine-based system that can, for human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments (perceive / abstract into models / model inference), including generative AI. Artificially generated sexual depiction: visual depiction that appears to authentically depict an individual in nudity or sexual conduct that did not occur in reality, production substantially dependent on technical means including AI or photo-editing software rather than physical impersonation. Generative AI: models that emulate training data to generate derived synthetic content
summary: HB 1364 (signed 5 May 2025, in force 1 Nov 2025) amends 21 O.S. 1040.13b to cover dissemination of artificially generated sexual depictions without effective consent, with intent or reckless disregard to harm. Base misdemeanor <=1 year/<=$1,000; financial-gain and 3-in-6-months felonies. ICS carve-out. Crime only; no PRA. No Oklahoma election-deepfake statute (HB 3299 / SB 894 failed). No insurance-code AI UR statute found.

citation_bill: Okla. Stat. tit. 75A, sections 300-320 (SB 546, 2026) — Oklahoma Consumer Data Privacy Act
short_title: OCDPA — profiling opt-out
operative_date: 2027-01-01; assessments of processing created after the effective date and shall not be retroactive
who_regulated: Controller or processor who conducts business in this state or produces a product or service targeted to residents and meets a threshold
hook: ADS / solely automated profiling in furtherance of a decision that produces a legal or similarly significant effect (includes insurance)
carve_outs: State agency/political subdivision and their processors; GLBA FI or data; HIPAA covered entity/BA; nonprofit; higher ed; purely personal/household processing; listed CSA listed-chemical data. PHI and listed health/research categories
enforcer: Attorney General exclusive authority (tit. 75A 312/313 as numbered in enrolled sections 13-14)
private_suit: none — express: shall not be construed as providing a basis for or being subject to a PRA (enrolled section 14(E))
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages. Civil penalty <= $7,500 for each violation after failed cure / breached cure statement
cure_period: permanent 30-day written notice before AG action (enrolled section 13)
fee_shifting: AG may recover fees/expenses (enrolled section 14) — not a private fee-shift
nexus: conducts business in this state or produces a product or service targeted to the residents of this state
out_of_state_actor: produces a product or service targeted to the residents of this state
insurance_situs: n/a — profiling legal-effect category includes insurance; GLBA entity carve-out; not an insurance-code UR statute
thresholds: during a calendar year: >=100,000 consumers, or >=25,000 consumers and >50% gross revenue from sale of personal data
retroactivity: assessments of processing created after the effective date and shall not be retroactive
ai_definition: Profiling: any form of solely automated processing (enrolled definitions). Not a GenAI definition
impact_assessment_discoverable: assessments available to the AG upon written request; compliance with an AG request shall not constitute a waiver (assessment section)
summary: SB 546 (signed 20 Mar 2026) creates the Oklahoma Consumer Data Privacy Act in Title 75A, effective 1 Jan 2027. Opt-out of solely automated profiling for legal/similarly significant effects, including insurance. AG exclusive; express no PRA; permanent 30-day cure; <=$7,500/violation. GLBA FI carve-out. Assessments not retroactive. Not an insurance-code UR statute.

short_title: Sexual exploitation / unlawful transmission — artificially generated visual depictions of children
effective_date: 2026-07-01 (publication in the statute book / legislature site)
who_regulated: Persons who possess, promote, or transmit visual depictions of children in sexually explicit conduct or nudity, including artificially generated / AI-altered depictions
hook: CSAM — artificially generated visual depiction; visual depiction includes AI-created/altered images purporting to depict a child, including with no actual child involved
carve_outs: 21-5510: possession of a visual depiction of a child in nudity if the possessor is that child. 21-5611: transmission by the depicted child; does not apply to sexually explicit conduct/obscenity (those stay in 21-5510). Preexisting 21-5610/5611 cross-cites retained
enforcer: criminal prosecution
private_suit: none in HB 2183
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages
nexus: silent
retroactivity: effective 2026-07-01 on statute-book publication — not a general retroactivity clause
criminal_overlay: also crime (21-5510 severity level 5/3/off-grid as amended; 21-5611 misdemeanor/felony grid as amended)
ai_definition: Artificially generated visual depiction: a visual depiction that is obscene and produced through computer software, digital manipulation, or other means that creates an image or video that appears to depict a child under 18 shown or heard engaging in sexually explicit conduct, including indistinguishable-from-real, morphed-from-real, or generated without any actual child. Visual depiction includes any photograph/film/video/digital/computer-generated image created, altered, or modified in whole or in part by artificial intelligence or any digital means to appear to depict or purport to depict a child engaging in sexually explicit conduct
summary: HB 2183 (approved 5 Feb 2026, in force 1 Jul 2026) amends K.S.A. 21-5510 so sexual exploitation includes possessing an artificially generated visual depiction and so visual depiction includes AI-created or AI-altered images of a child, including with no actual child involved. Parallel CGI/AI language is added to 21-5611 (unlawful transmission). Crime only. Adult NCII AI language in 21-6101(a)(8) is a separate row. SB 525 deepfake PRA died in committee 2024. SB 375 election GenAI died.

short_title: Breach of privacy — AI-altered nude or sexual images of identifiable adults
who_regulated: A person who disseminates a videotape/photograph/film/image of an identifiable person 18+ who is nude or engaged in sexual activity, without consent, with intent to harass/threaten/intimidate, including AI-created/altered images purporting to depict that person whether or not the person was involved in creating the original image
hook: Intimate deepfake / AI-altered nude or sexual image of an identifiable adult (criminal breach of privacy)
carve_outs: ICS (47 U.S.C. 230) for content provided by another; telco/radio-common-carrier/LEC; cable service (47 U.S.C. 522); DTH satellite (47 U.S.C. 303(v)); MVPD. (a)(8) does not apply to a person acting with a bona fide and lawful scientific, educational, governmental, news, or other similar public purpose
enforcer: criminal prosecution
private_suit: none in 21-6101 / HB 2183 (criminal only; SB 525 civil deepfake PRA not enacted)
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated damages. (a)(8) is a severity level 8 person felony (level 5 on second/subsequent within 5 years)
nexus: silent
retroactivity: effective 2026-07-01 — not a general retroactivity clause
ai_definition: (a)(8) includes disseminating any videotape, photograph, film, or image that has been created, in whole or in part, altered or modified by artificial intelligence or any digital means to appear to depict or purport to depict such identifiable person, regardless of whether such identifiable person was involved in the creation of the original image
summary: The same HB 2183 that expanded child-exploitation CGI also amended K.S.A. 21-6101(a)(8) so criminal breach-of-privacy dissemination of nude/sexual images of identifiable adults covers AI-created or AI-altered images even if the depicted person was not in the original. Severity level 8 person felony (level 5 repeat in 5 years). ICS and news/public-purpose carve-outs. Crime only; Kansas still has no BIPA-style or SB 525-style private liquidated deepfake statute.

citation_bill: 3 V.S.A. §§ 3305, 5022–5023 (2021, No. 132 (Adj. Sess.), H.410; council later amended, incl. 2026 Acts Nos. 101, 156)
short_title: Division of Artificial Intelligence; state ADS inventory
status: in force (council sunset extended to 2030-06-30 by Act 101)

short_title: Nonconsensual sexually explicit images (digitization / computer-generated)
who_regulated: Person who knowingly discloses an identifiable visual image of a person nude or engaged in sexual conduct
hook: Intimate-image / deepfake-adjacent: visual image includes digital reproduction created or altered by digitization; digitization uses images of a person (including someone other than the person depicted) or computer-generated images. Offense + PRA.
carve_outs: Voluntary public/commercial nudity; public-interest/law-enforcement/legal/medical disclosures; matters of public concern; ICS/information/telecom for content solely provided by another (not precluding other remedies) (§ 2606(d))
enforcer: Prosecuting authority; depicted plaintiff (PRA)
private_suit: PRA — plaintiff vs knowing nonconsensual disclosure causing harm (§ 2606(e)); equitable relief including injunction/pseudonym
statutory_damages: none as liquidated floor in § 2606(e). Offense: ≤2 years / ≤$2,000; profit-intent ≤5 years / ≤$10,000
nexus: silent
retroactivity: Act 89 effective 2026-07-01; digitization amendment 2024-06-06 — not a general retroactivity clause
limitations_period: Act 89 extends criminal limitations for § 2606 (compiled 2025 text still shows prior period; confirm 2026 compile). Civil limitations silent in § 2606(e)
ai_definition: Digitization: altering an image in a realistic manner utilizing an image or images of a person, including images other than the person depicted, or computer-generated images (§ 2606(a)(6)). Statute does not say artificial intelligence.
summary: § 2606 covers realistic computer-generated/digitized identifiable nude or sexual-conduct images. Knowing disclosure with harm intent is an offense (2 years/$2,000; 5 years/$10,000 if for profit). Depicted plaintiff has a PRA for knowing nonconsensual disclosure causing harm, plus injunction. No liquidated civil floor. Digitization definition 6 Jun 2024; Act 89 signed 28 Apr 2026 effective 1 Jul 2026.

short_title: Use of synthetic media in elections
who_regulated: Person who, within 90 days before a Vermont election, publishes/communicates/distributes synthetic media the person knows is deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media
hook: Election synthetic media (incl. AI): required disclosure that the media has been manipulated or generated by digital technology and depicts speech or conduct that did not occur.
carve_outs: Bona fide news with authenticity acknowledgment; paid broadcast; federal candidate-ad carriage; newspapers/periodicals of general interest with accuracy statement; satire/parody; telecom/information service and ICS for content provided by another (§ 2032(b))
enforcer: State's Attorney or Attorney General (injunction/other proceeding, civil investigation) (§§ 2041–2042). Candidate PAG for injunction/equitable relief only (§ 2033(b))
private_suit: PAG — candidate whose appearance/speech/conduct/environment is misrepresented may seek injunctive or other equitable relief (§ 2033(b)). No damages PRA in the act
statutory_damages: none as private liquidated. Knowing/intentional violation: fine ≤$1,000; ≤$5,000 if intent to cause violence/bodily harm; ≤$10,000 if prior within 5 years; ≤$15,000 if both. Investigation obstruction ≤$5,000
nexus: 90 days before an election in Vermont; AG/SA may take testimony in Washington County if nonresident or no Vermont place of business (§ 2042(a)(2))
out_of_state_actor: civil investigation attendance in Washington County if nonresident/no VT place of business (§ 2042(a)(2))
ai_definition: Synthetic media: image, audio, or video of an individual's appearance, speech, or conduct created or intentionally manipulated with digital technology, including artificial intelligence (§ 2031(2)). Deceptive and fraudulent: realistic representation of a political candidate that injures reputation, or of an individual that attempts to unduly influence an election (incl. public question) by materially false information (§ 2031(1))
summary: Act 75 (S.23, signed 5 Mar 2026, on passage) requires a disclosure for knowing distribution of deceptive/fraudulent synthetic media (incl. AI) within 90 days of a Vermont election. Candidate may seek injunction/equitable relief only. AG or State's Attorney may sue and investigate. Fines up to $1,000 (higher with violence intent or recidivism). News, satire, ICS/telecom excepted.

No PRA and no private-sector mandate in § 1891. Council sunset extended to 30 Jun 2030.

retroactivity: operative 2028-01-01; not a general retroactivity clause
ai_definition: Profiling / ADS opt-out; biometric data is sensitive. Act does not create a general AI definition beyond privacy/profiling terms.
impact_assessment_discoverable: data protection assessments as provided in the act (discoverability vs AG — see enrolled; silent here if unsaid)
summary: Act 145 (S.71, signed 16 Jun 2026) enacts the Vermont Data Privacy Act, operative 1 Jan 2028. AG-only enforcement with 60-day cure through 30 Jun 2029. Express no PRA. 8 V.S.A. part 3 insurers and GLBA entities/data carved out. Biometrics are sensitive data; no BIPA-style PRA.

carve_outs: State/political subdivision; GLBA financial institution, affiliate, or Title V data; HIPAA covered entity/BA; nonprofit; IHE; electric/natural-gas utilities (87-1103(2)). Information exemptions in 87-1104.
enforcer: Attorney General exclusive (87-1119)
private_suit: none
statutory_damages: AG civil penalty not to exceed $7,500 per violation after cure (87-1124); not a consumer PRA floor
cure_period: 30-day AG written notice/cure before action (87-1122); no sunset in compiled text reviewed
fee_shifting: AG may recover fees/expenses of investigation and action (87-1124)
nexus: conducts business in this state or produces a product or service consumed by residents of this state (87-1103(1)(a))
out_of_state_actor: applies if produces product/service consumed by NE residents (87-1103(1)(a))
insurance_situs: n/a — profiling legal-effect category may include insurance-type decisions; GLBA FI/data entity carve-out. Not an insurance-code UR statute.
thresholds: not a small business under federal Small Business Act as of 2024-01-01 (87-1103(1)(c))
safe_harbor: 30-day cure; comparable other-law assessments may satisfy
ai_definition: Profiling: any form of solely automated processing of personal data to evaluate/analyze/predict personal aspects (economic situation, health, preferences, interests, reliability, behavior, location, or movements) (87-1102(25))
impact_assessment_discoverable: AG may demand data-protection assessment via CID (87-1121); not a public-discovery clause
summary: NDPA (in force 1 Jan 2025) gives NE consumers an opt-out of solely automated profiling that produces legal or similarly significant effects, plus assessments for high-risk profiling. Biometric data is sensitive (consent; no private liquidated BIPA). AG exclusive; $7,500/violation after a standing 30-day cure. GLBA FI/data and HIPAA CE/BA are entity-out. Not insurance-code UR.

citation_bill: Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 25-3502–25-3505 (LB 371, 2025) Uniform Civil Remedies for Unauthorized Disclosure of Intimate Images Act (computer-generation amendment)
short_title: Intimate-image civil remedies — computer generation / digital manipulation
effective_date: unconfirmed — NE default three months after adjournment unless specified; confirm slip effective clause
operative_date: unconfirmed (treat as in force by 2026-09-02 if default ran; confirm)
who_regulated: Person who intentionally discloses or threatens disclosure of a private intimate image
hook: Depicted individual includes computer generation or digital manipulation; private includes images created by computer generation or digital manipulation without consent. Civil PRA for identifiable depicted individual who suffers harm.
carve_outs: 25-3504 exceptions (existing uniform-act exemptions; not re-pulled this pass)
enforcer: private plaintiff; public enforcer unsaid in 25-3503
private_suit: PRA
statutory_damages: presumed damages not to exceed $10,000 per defendant if actual damages hard to quantify (25-3505(a)(1)(B)); plus economic/noneconomic including emotional distress; plus defendant monetary gain
fee_shifting: court may award prevailing plaintiff reasonable attorney fees and costs (25-3505(b))
nexus: silent in 25-3503
limitations_period: lead: 4 years from discovery under original uniform act / 25-3508 — confirm 25-3508 not amended by LB 371
ai_definition: no standalone AI definition; computer generation or digital manipulation (25-3503(a)(2)(C))
summary: LB 371 (signed 30 May 2025) amends the uniform intimate-image civil act so identifiable depicted individuals include computer-generated or digitally manipulated images, and private includes those created that way without consent. Prevailing plaintiff: actual or presumed damages up to $10,000/defendant, disgorgement, fees, injunction. Slip PDF TLS-failed this pass; default effective date unconfirmed.

who_regulated: Operators of public conversational AI services (definitions unconfirmed — slip/engrossed PDF TLS-failed)

nexus: unconfirmed
