citation_bill: Ark. Code §§ 4-75-1103, 4-75-1110, 4-75-1112 (Act 159 / HB 1071, 2025) Frank Broyles Publicity Rights Protection Act AI amendments
short_title: Publicity rights — AI photograph / voice / likeness
effective_date: 2025-08-03 (AR default 90th day after 2025-05-05 sine die; no emergency clause on the 3-page act)
who_regulated: Person making unauthorized commercial use of name, voice, signature, photograph, or likeness
hook: Likeness, photograph, and voice definitions now include generation/simulation through artificial intelligence. Property rights not IP for 47 U.S.C. 230 (4-75-1112(b)).
carve_outs: Existing 4-75-1110 exemptions (news, etc.) not rewritten except actual-knowledge tweak for service providers regarding photograph, voice, or likeness
enforcer: private plaintiff (4-75-1109)
private_suit: PRA
statutory_damages: none in 4-75-1109 — actual damages plus attributable profits; no liquidated floor
nexus: civil action in county where defendant resides or violation occurred (4-75-1109)
retroactivity: does not invalidate contracts transferring rights before or after 2016-08-22 (4-75-1112(a)(2))
safe_harbor: service-provider exemption if no actual knowledge of violating photograph/voice/likeness (4-75-1110 as amended)
federal_preemption: not IP for section 230 (4-75-1112(b)) — not a preemption clause
ai_definition: no standalone AI definition; generation through means of artificial intelligence in likeness/photograph/voice defs
summary: Act 159 (approved 25 Feb 2025) folds AI-generated image/video/3D and AI-simulated voice into the Broyles publicity-rights definitions. Existing PRA: injunction, actual damages, and profits; no statutory floor, no fees in 1109. Default effective about 3 Aug 2025. States the rights are not IP for section 230.

short_title: Deepfake visual material of a sexual nature — crime and civil action
effective_date: 2025-08-03 (default 90 days after sine die; no emergency on act)
who_regulated: Person who knowingly creates or distributes nonconsensual deepfake visual material of an identifiable person; providers/developers of prompt-based image-generation technology used to create it
hook: Crime: create/distribute deepfake visual material of identifiable person in a state of nudity or engaging in sexual conduct without consent. PRA vs creator or vs provider/developer of the image-generation tech. AG civil vs prompt-based image-gen provider/developer lacking reasonable safeguards.
carve_outs: Telecom/information/cable service providers (47 U.S.C. 153) for content provided by another (5-14-139(d))
enforcer: prosecutors (crime); AG civil vs image-gen providers; injured person PRA
private_suit: PRA
statutory_damages: none — actual, compensatory, punitive, injunctive, or other appropriate relief (16-118-119(b)(2)); no liquidated floor
fee_shifting: prevailing plaintiff shall be awarded reasonable attorney fees and costs (16-118-119(b)(3))
nexus: silent
safe_harbor: ICS/telecom for others content; AG action requires lack of reasonable safeguards on prompt-based image gen
criminal_overlay: also crime — Class A misdemeanor first; Class D felony subsequent (5-14-139(c))
ai_definition: Deepfake visual material: photograph/image/video/other visual that appears authentic of an identifiable person and is generated, modified, or adapted using technology to falsely depict appearance, voice, or conduct. AI unsaid in the definition.
summary: Act 827 (17 Apr 2025) criminalizes nonconsensual sexual deepfake visuals (A misd / D felony) and creates a PRA for actual/compensatory/punitive damages plus mandatory plaintiff fees against the creator or the image-gen provider/developer. AG may sue prompt-based image-gen providers without reasonable safeguards. Default effective about 3 Aug 2025.

short_title: Public-entity AI and automated-decision-tool policy
who_regulated: Public entities (listed state departments, political subdivisions, public schools, IHEs, constitutional officers, highway/game commissions, etc.)
hook: Must adopt an AI and automated-decision-tool policy defining authorized use and requiring an authorized human employee/designee to make any final employment decision regardless of AI/ADT recommendation; training; public availability of state-entity policies; disciplinary procedure.
carve_outs: Cybersecurity-policy training carve for political subdivisions only (not the AI policy duty). No private-sector coverage.
enforcer: unconfirmed — internal disciplinary procedure; no PRA/AG clause in the amended subsections
private_suit: none in the amended text
statutory_damages: none
nexus: public entity as defined (taxpayer-funded instrumentalities listed)
ai_definition: AI: machine-based system that can, based on a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing a real or virtual environment. Automated decision tool: system/service using AI specifically developed and marketed, or specifically modified, to make or be a controlling factor in making consequential decisions.
summary: Act 848 (17 Apr 2025) requires listed public entities to adopt AI/ADT use policies with a human making every final employment decision, train staff, and (for state entities) make the policy available on request. Government-use only. No PRA. Default effective about 3 Aug 2025.

short_title: Computer-generated images of a child — AI definition in exploitation offenses
who_regulated: Persons who advertise, sell, distribute, possess, or view matter depicting a child in sexually explicit conduct, including computer-generated images indistinguishable from a child
hook: Computer generated / computer generated image means produced, adapted, or modified in whole or in part through AI. Offenses cover images indistinguishable from an actual child. Crime track.
carve_outs: Law-enforcement investigation possession/viewing; ICS (47 U.S.C. 230) for others content and for good-faith adversarial testing with an AI developer to prevent prohibited generation (not personal/exploitative testing)
enforcer: criminal prosecution
private_suit: none in Act 977
statutory_damages: none (crime)
nexus: silent
ai_definition: Computer generated means produced, adapted, or modified, in whole or in part, through the use of artificial intelligence. Indistinguishable: ordinary person would conclude the medium depicts an actual child; excludes drawing/cartoon/sculpture/painting.
summary: Act 977 (22 Apr 2025) defines computer-generated prohibited child imagery as AI-produced/adapted/modified and extends related offenses to indistinguishable synthetic images of a child. ICS red-team carve-out. Crime only. Default effective about 3 Aug 2025.

short_title: Election materially deceptive media
who_regulated: Person who recklessly distributes, or agrees to distribute, materially deceptive media in the even-year February-through-general-election window
hook: Ban on reckless distribution of AI/GAN/digital-tech election advertisements that falsely depict speech/conduct, in reckless disregard of harm to candidate reputation/electoral prospects or changing voting behavior. Disclaimer safe harbor. Crime plus PRA for general/special damages and injunction.
carve_outs: Broadcaster/cable/DTH unless involved in creation; ICS/cloud/streaming for others content unless knowledge it is deceptive and intent to deceive a Hawaii resident; qualifying disclaimer plus original-source citation for edited media
enforcer: Campaign Spending Commission (fine or criminal referral); AG, CSC, county attorney/prosecutor (injunction); depicted individual/candidate/voter org (damages and injunction)
private_suit: PRA (depicted individual including candidate; voter-interest organization) — general or special damages; also injunction PAG
statutory_damages: none for the underlying violation; civil fine not more than $1,000/day for violating a court order (11-304(b))
fee_shifting: court may award a prevailing party reasonable attorney fees and costs on damages action; may award fees to non-government plaintiff awarded permanent injunction
nexus: intent to deceive a resident of the State is an ICS knowledge qualifier; distribution during HI election window
criminal_overlay: also crime — petty misdemeanor; misdemeanor within 5 years of prior; class C felony if intent to cause violence or bodily harm (11-303(d)-(f))
litigation_status: silent (secondary reports of litigation are not holdings)
ai_definition: AI: machine-based system that can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments, using machine and human-based inputs to perceive, model, and infer. Materially deceptive media must be created by GAN/ML/CNN, AI, or digital technology.
summary: Act 191 (2024, upon approval) bans reckless distribution of AI/GAN election deepfake ads from the first working day of February in even years through the general election, with a disclaimer safe harbor. Petty misd / misd / C felony. Depicted individuals, candidates, and voter orgs may sue for general/special damages and injunction; $1,000/day only for violating a court order. Fees discretionary.

citation_bill: Haw. Rev. Stat. new chapter (Act 247 / HB 2137 HD3 SD2 CD1, 2026) — compiled chapter number unconfirmed
short_title: Realistic digital imitations — civil deepfake
who_regulated: Person who knowingly publishes a realistic AI-generated digital imitation of an identifiable individual without consent
hook: Unlawful to knowingly publish a realistic digital imitation used in an advertisement, causing harm, or used to commit fraud/defamation/harassment/other crime. PRA: injunction; up to $25,000 per advertisement or actual damages (reputational/emotional); punitive if malice; fees/costs. AG may seek injunction for broad public interest/widespread harm.
carve_outs: Parody/satire/commentary/criticism/scholarship/political or educational expression; news illustration; documentary/historical/biographical (incl. some fictionalization); ads for those works if relevant. Medium disseminating third-party content for the dissemination role only. Section 230 savings.
enforcer: depicted individual or estate (10 years after death); AG for equitable relief in broad-harm cases
private_suit: PRA
statutory_damages: up to $25,000 per advertisement or actual damages (plaintiff election in CD1 sec. -4(b)(2))
fee_shifting: reasonable attorneys fees and court costs to the individual/estate (CD1 sec. -4(b)(4))
nexus: silent beyond publication of imitation of an individual (CD1 does not state a HI-resident limit)
retroactivity: does not affect rights/duties/penalties/proceedings begun before effective date (Act sec. 4)
limitations_period: does not extend chapter 657; estate may sue up to 10 years after death
safe_harbor: expressive/news/historical exemptions; distributor medium exemption; section 230
criminal_overlay: civil-only (this act); publication used to commit other crimes is an element, not a new crime
federal_preemption: applies to fullest extent permitted by federal law; section 230 savings
ai_definition: AI: machine-based system that can, for human-defined objectives, make predictions/recommendations/decisions influencing real or virtual environments (perceive/model/infer). Digital imitation: highly realistic AI-generated depiction/audio/video derived from identifying characteristics portraying voice/face/likeness in a work in which the individual did not perform or appear. Realistic: so lifelike a reasonable person would believe it authentic.
summary: Act 247 (signed 14 Jul 2026, immediate) creates a civil ban on knowingly publishing nonconsensual realistic AI imitations in ads, causing harm, or used for fraud/defamation/harassment/crime. PRA: injunction, up to $25,000/ad or actuals, punitive for malice, fees. Parody/news/historical and distributor exemptions. Compiled HRS chapter number unconfirmed.

citation_bill: Haw. Rev. Stat. § 481B-__ (Act 248 / SB 3001 SD2 HD3 CD1, 2026) Artificial Intelligence Disclosure and Safety Act
short_title: AI Disclosure and Safety Act — AI companions
status: in force (duties upon approval; annual reports from 2028-01-01)
who_regulated: Operator who develops and makes available an AI companion to the public (app stores/search engines that merely provide access are not operators)
hook: If a reasonable person would think the companion is human, clear conspicuous notice it is AI. Heightened minor disclosures (persistent or start-of-session plus hourly). Crisis protocol; no professional MH claims; no engagement-reward tricks or sexual outputs to known minors; annual DOH reports from 2028.
carve_outs: Developer of an AI model not liable for a third party companion built on it. App store/search engine mere access is not operator.
enforcer: UDAP HRS 480-2 (public); express no PRA
private_suit: none — nothing in this section shall be interpreted as creating a private right of action to enforce this section or to support a private right of action under any other law
statutory_damages: none in Act 248; 480-2 public UDAP penalties not restated here (unconfirmed amounts)
fee_shifting: silent in Act 248 (UDAP fee rules unimported)
nexus: operators of AI companions; CD1 does not add a separate HI-user threshold beyond making available / interacting
retroactivity: does not affect rights/duties/penalties/proceedings begun before effective date
ai_definition: AI: engineered or machine-based system that varies in autonomy and can, for explicit or implicit objectives, infer from input how to generate outputs that can influence physical or virtual environments. AI companion: system using AI/GenAI/emotional-recognition designed to simulate a sustained human-like relationship (retain session prefs; unprompted emotion questions; ongoing personal dialogue).
impact_assessment_discoverable: n/a; annual aggregate reports to DOH Behavioral Health Administration (no user identifiers)
record_retention: annual reports from 2028-01-01; no year-count retention for chats
summary: Act 248 (14 Jul 2026, immediate) regulates public AI companions: human-perception disclosure, minor hourly reminders, crisis referrals, no MH-professional claims, minor sexual/engagement limits, DOH reports from 2028. Violations are 480-2 UDAP; express no PRA. Penalty dollars not in the CD1.

citation_bill: R.I. Gen. Laws § 11-64-3 (P.L. 2025, ch. 429 / S 0136; companion ch. 430 / H 5046)
short_title: Unauthorized dissemination of indecent material — digitization
who_regulated: Person who intentionally disseminates, publishes, or sells a sexually explicit visual image of an identifiable person 18 or older, including images created by a digital device or altered by digitization
hook: Crime covers images created by a digital device or altered by digitization, made/obtained under privacy circumstances or created without consent, disseminated without consent, with knowledge/reckless disregard of harm or intent to harass.
carve_outs: Voluntary public/commercial exposure; public-interest/scientific/educational; lawful public proceeding; law enforcement/legal/medical; public-concern/newsworthy/public-figure. ICS/information/telecom for others content. No sex-offender registration for this section.
enforcer: criminal prosecution
private_suit: none in ch. 429 as enrolled
statutory_damages: criminal fines: up to $1,000 first (misd); up to $3,000 subsequent (felony); threat/extortion felonies up to $5,000 — not a civil PRA floor
nexus: offense committed in RI if any element or any harm to the depicted person occurs in this state (11-64-3(h))
out_of_state_actor: yes if harm in RI or an element in RI
criminal_overlay: crime-only — misd 1 year/$1,000 first; felony 3 years/$3,000 subsequent; threat/pay-to-remove felonies 5 years/$5,000
ai_definition: no AI definition; covers image created by a digital device or altered by digitization
summary: P.L. 2025 ch. 429 (2 Jul 2025, immediate) expands RI indecent-image crime to digital-device-created and digitized/altered images of identifiable adults, with a harm-in-state nexus. Crime only; ICS carve; no PRA in the enrolled chapter.

short_title: Deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media in election communications
who_regulated: Candidate, authorized campaign committee, PAC, party committee, or independent-expenditure entity
hook: Within 90 days of an election, may not distribute deceptive synthetic media (GAN/digital-tech realistic false image/audio/video of appearance, speech, or conduct) unless it includes a disclosure that it was manipulated or generated by AI.
carve_outs: Disclosure safe harbor with specified size/duration/audio-interval rules. Does not regulate private citizens who are not IE makers (statute lists only political actors). Satire/parody — confirm remaining 17-30-1 subsections.
enforcer: candidate PRA (injunction and damages). Board of Elections unsaid in 17-30-2.
private_suit: PRA (candidate only)
statutory_damages: none — general or special damages; no floor
fee_shifting: court may award a prevailing party reasonable attorneys fees and costs (17-30-2(b))
notice_cure: disclosure exception is a safe harbor, not a cure letter
nexus: 90 days of a RI election at which a candidate appears on the ballot
out_of_state_actor: silent (covers listed political actors distributing in that window)
safe_harbor: AI disclosure; plaintiff must prove violation by clear and convincing evidence (17-30-2(c))
ai_definition: Synthetic media: image/audio/video of an individual appearance, speech, or conduct intentionally manipulated with GAN techniques or other digital technology to create a realistic but false image/audio/video. Disclosure refers to artificial intelligence.
summary: P.L. 2025 chs. 409/410 (2 Jul 2025) bar candidates/committees/IE spenders from undisclosed deceptive synthetic media within 90 days of an election. Candidates may seek injunction and general/special damages (C&C; fees discretionary). No liquidated floor. Not a general deepfake ban.

citation_bill: R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 23-106 or 23-108 (P.L. 2026, ch. 372 / S 2570A) Use of Artificial Intelligence by Healthcare Providers Notification Act
short_title: Healthcare AI scribe notification
who_regulated: Healthcare providers (listed licensed professionals) and healthcare facilities (section 23-17-2) that employ AI to document in-person or telehealth visits
hook: Must notify patients of AI used solely to document the visit and review AI-generated documentation for accuracy after the visit. No other AI uses (imaging/CDS) are covered.
carve_outs: Applies only to visit documentation, not other clinical AI
enforcer: unconfirmed — no penalty/enforcer section in the enrolled chapter
private_suit: unconfirmed (none in enrolled chapter)
statutory_damages: none in enrolled chapter
notice_cure: patient notification is the duty, not a cure period
nexus: RI-licensed providers and RI healthcare facilities
ai_definition: any technology that can simulate human intelligence including NLP, training language models, RLHF, and machine learning systems
summary: P.L. 2026 ch. 372 (22 Jun 2026, immediate) requires licensed providers and facilities using AI to document visits to notify the patient and review the note for accuracy. Enforcer/PRA/penalties unsaid. Compiled chapter number printed as 106108 on the public-law HTML (likely 23-106 or 23-108).

citation_bill: R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 40.1-5.5 (P.L. 2026 / S 2197Aaa and H 7349 companion) Oversight of Artificial Intelligence Technology in Mental Health Care Act
short_title: Oversight of AI in mental health care
enacted_date: 2026-06-22 (governor signing day for the 2026 AI health package)
who_regulated: Licensed professionals/providers of therapy or psychotherapy; anyone offering/advertising therapy to the public in RI, including via internet AI
hook: May not offer therapy unless conducted by a RI-licensed professional. Licensed professionals may not use AI to make independent therapeutic decisions, determine treatment plans, or (without an established relationship) directly interact in therapeutic communication. Companion/emotional-support AI in recorded sessions needs specific written consent. EOHHS investigates.
carve_outs: Religious counseling; peer support; public self-help that does not purport to be therapy; FDA/federal-cleared AI tools; IRB research under specified CFR. Administrative support (scheduling/billing) vs supplementary support definitions.
enforcer: EOHHS investigation; confidentiality penalties via section 5-37.3-9
private_suit: unconfirmed (none in S2197Aaa as enrolled)
statutory_damages: confidentiality path uses section 5-37.3-9 (not restated here)
notice_cure: written consent for recorded-session companion AI is a permission condition, not a cure
nexus: offer therapy or psychotherapy services to the public in this state, including internet-based AI
out_of_state_actor: covers offering therapy to the public in this state via internet AI
criminal_overlay: unconfirmed (penalty section points to confidentiality statute)
ai_definition: machine-based system that can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments
summary: S 2197Aaa (upon passage 22 Jun 2026) bans unlicensed AI therapy offered to the RI public and bars licensed clinicians from using AI for independent therapeutic decisions or unsupervised therapeutic chat. Consent required for companion AI on recorded sessions. EOHHS enforces; no PRA in the enrolled text.

citation_bill: R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 6-63 (P.L. 2026 / S 2195Aaa and H 7350 companion) Artificial Intelligence Companion Models
short_title: AI companion models — crisis protocol and notice
who_regulated: Operator who operates or provides an AI companion (person/partnership/firm and members/affiliates/subsidiaries/beneficial owners)
hook: Must include protocols for user suicidal ideation/self-harm and physical harm to others, with crisis-service referral when detected. Clear conspicuous notice at start of interaction and at least every 3 hours that the user is not communicating with a human. Annual AG reports from 2027-07-01.
carve_outs: Customer-service-only systems; efficiency/research/technical-assistance systems; internal/employee-productivity systems
enforcer: Attorney General (investigate, sue, injunctions)
private_suit: none in enrolled chapter
statutory_damages: civil penalties up to $15,000 per day, directed to suicide-prevention programs (6-63-4(b)) — public penalty, not a consumer PRA floor
nexus: user who uses an AI companion within the state (6-63-1(8))
out_of_state_actor: operator providing a companion used by a person within the state
ai_definition: AI: machine-based system that can, for human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments. AI companion: system using AI/GenAI/emotional-recognition to simulate a sustained human-like relationship (retain prefs; unprompted emotion questions; ongoing personal dialogue).
impact_assessment_discoverable: n/a; annual protocol-activation metrics to AG (aggregated publication)
record_retention: annual reports from 2027-07-01; no chat-retention year count
summary: S 2195Aaa (signed with the 22 Jun 2026 package; operative 1 Jan 2027) requires AI-companion operators to run crisis protocols, disclose non-human status at start and every 3 hours, and report to the AG from 1 Jul 2027. AG-only; up to $15,000/day to suicide-prevention programs. No PRA.

citation_bill: 10 M.R.S. § 1500-DD (P.L. 2025, c. 294 / LD 1727; reallocated from § 1500-Y)
short_title: Required disclosure of AI chatbot in trade and commerce
effective_date: 2025-09-16 (lead — 90 days after 132nd First Special adjournment; confirm calendar)
who_regulated: Person using an AI chatbot or other computer technology to engage in trade and commerce with a consumer
hook: May not use an AI chatbot (or other computer technology) in trade/commerce in a manner that may mislead or deceive a reasonable consumer into believing they are engaging with a human, unless clear and conspicuous notice that they are not.
carve_outs: none in section 1500-DD
enforcer: UTPA (AG and private under 5 M.R.S. sections 207, 213)
private_suit: PAG via Maine UTPA section 213 — purchaser/lessee of goods/services/property primarily for personal/family/household use who suffers loss of money or property; actual damages, restitution, equitable relief; 30-day pre-suit demand
statutory_damages: none in UTPA section 213 (actual damages/restitution; no liquidated floor)
cure_period: 30-day written demand for relief before filing for damages (5 M.R.S. section 213(1-A)); not a statutory cure of the violation
fee_shifting: if court finds section 207 violation, petitioner shall be awarded reasonable attorney fees and costs (5 M.R.S. section 213(2))
nexus: trade and commerce with a consumer (Title 5 section 206(3) meanings)
limitations_period: UTPA private actions generally 6 years (lead; not restated in 1500-DD)
safe_harbor: clear conspicuous notice that the consumer is not engaging with a human
ai_definition: Artificial intelligence chatbot: software application, web interface, or computer program that simulates human conversation and interaction through textual or aural communications
summary: P.L. 2025 c. 294 requires clear conspicuous disclosure when an AI chatbot (or other computer tech) in trade/commerce might reasonably be mistaken for a human. Violation is Maine UTPA: consumer PRA for actual damages/restitution after a 30-day demand; mandatory fees if violation found. No statutory floor. Default effective about 16 Sep 2025.

short_title: Unauthorized dissemination of private images — created or modified images
effective_date: unconfirmed — 90 days after adjournment unless specified (confirm chapter effective)
operative_date: unconfirmed (in force by 2026-09-02 if default ran)
who_regulated: Person who, with intent to harass/torment/threaten, intentionally or knowingly disseminates/displays/publishes a private image
hook: Crime now covers an image created or modified so it appears to show the depicted person in nudity or a sexual act/contact. New image definition includes generated/saved computer data files and mechanically/electronically/chemically reproduced visuals.
carve_outs: Medical treatment; voluntary public/commercial exposure; ICS/information service for content provided by another
enforcer: criminal prosecution
private_suit: none in section 511-A (protection-from-abuse cross-defs in c. 400 not separately pulled as a PRA)
statutory_damages: none (Class D crime)
nexus: silent in section 511-A
thresholds: identifiable from the image or accompanying information; no consent
ai_definition: no AI definition; covers images created or modified so they appear to show nudity/sexual conduct; image includes generated computer data files
record_retention: court-record access governed by SJC rule (subsection 5)
summary: P.L. 2025 c. 400 amends Maine Class D private-image crime to include created or modified (synthetic) depictions of nudity or sexual conduct of an identifiable unconsenting person, with harass/torment/threaten intent. ICS carve. No civil PRA in 511-A.

short_title: Fraudulent use of deepfakes — felony and civil action
who_regulated: Person who knowingly creates, distributes, or presents a deepfake of an identifiable individual for embarrassment, harassment, entrapment, defamation, extortion, or financial/reputational harm
hook: Class B felony for fraudulent deepfakes; separate Class B felony if the deepfake causes the depicted person arrest (plus defense-cost liability). Parallel PRA for damages from such use.
carve_outs: ICS for others content; bona fide news report that flags authenticity questions; paid election-communication publishers who keep the sponsor disclaimer; satire/parody or physical/verbal impersonation without reliance on AI
enforcer: criminal prosecution; private plaintiff (507:8-j)
statutory_damages: none — damages resulting from such use; no liquidated floor. Separate defense-cost liability if arrest results (638:26-a III).
fee_shifting: silent in 507:8-j (defense costs only in the arrest overlay, 638:26-a III)
nexus: silent
safe_harbor: news / ICS / satire / paid-ad disclaimer carves
criminal_overlay: also crime — Class B felony (and separate Class B if arrest results)
ai_definition: AI: ability of a machine to display human-like capabilities for cognitive tasks such as reasoning, learning, planning, and creativity; may adapt without significant human oversight. Deepfake: video/audio/other media of a person whose face/body/voice has been digitally altered so they appear to be someone else, or to say/do something they never said/did.
summary: RSA 638:26-a (Class B felony) and 507:8-j (damages PRA, no floor) cover knowing creation/distribution of deepfakes used to embarrass, harass, defame, extort, or cause financial/reputational harm. News/ICS/satire carves. Chapter/effective calendar lead 1 Jan 2025.

short_title: Synthetic media and deceptive/fraudulent deepfakes in elections
who_regulated: Person, corporation, committee, or other entity distributing a message within 90 days of an election
hook: Within 90 days of an election, may not distribute a message created using AI/GenAI that the distributor knows or should have known is a deepfake of a candidate, election official, or party on the ballot, unless a specified AI-manipulation disclosure is included. Candidate/election-official injunction and general/special damages vs sponsor.
carve_outs: ICS for others content; individual distributor who did not know and had no reasonable way of knowing it was a deepfake; bona fide news that flags authenticity; paid publishers who keep sponsor disclaimer; satire/parody or non-AI impersonation
enforcer: candidate or election official (injunction and damages vs sponsor)
private_suit: PRA (candidate or election official)
statutory_damages: none — general or special damages; no floor
fee_shifting: court may award a prevailing party reasonable attorneys fees and costs
notice_cure: disclosure is a safe harbor, not a cure letter
nexus: within 90 days of an election at which a candidate will appear on the ballot
safe_harbor: specified disclosure; lack of knowledge for individuals; news/ICS/satire
ai_definition: AI/GenAI/deepfake/synthetic media defined in 664:14-c I (GAN or other digital technology creating realistic but false image/audio/video; GenAI generates media in response to prompts; deepfake matches 638:26-a).
summary: RSA 664:14-c bars undisclosed AI/GenAI deepfakes of candidates, election officials, or parties within 90 days of an election. Depicted candidate/official may seek injunction and general/special damages against the sponsor, with discretionary fees. No liquidated floor. Enacted/effective calendar unconfirmed on the compiled page.

short_title: Use of artificial intelligence by state agencies
operative_date: 2024-07-01 (compliance review due 9 months after effective date)
who_regulated: State agencies (any department, commission, board, institution, bureau, office, law enforcement, or other entity including legislative and judicial branches) as to computer systems they operate
hook: Prohibits classifying persons in ways resulting in unlawful discrimination; real-time remote biometric ID surveillance in public spaces except law enforcement with a warrant; deceptive or malicious deepfakes. Human review before irreversible AI recommendations/decisions. Generative AI material must be disclosed if not human-reviewed; users must be told they are interacting with AI.
carve_outs: Research systems at state-funded IHEs; installed consumer systems in common personal use (e.g., phone unlock face ID)
enforcer: Department of Information Technology reporting; no PRA in chapter
private_suit: none in RSA 5-D
statutory_damages: none
nexus: computer systems operated by a NH state agency
retroactivity: newly deployed systems after effective date must comply; 9-month review of existing systems
ai_definition: AI: ability of a machine to display human-like capabilities for cognitive tasks (reasoning, learning, planning, creativity); may adapt without significant human oversight. Generative AI: AI that can generate text, images, or other media in response to prompts. Deepfake: digitally altered face/body/voice media.
impact_assessment_discoverable: DoIT annual public report of identified systems (not a litigation discovery clause)
record_retention: annual DoIT reports posted on website
summary: RSA 5-D (eff. 1 Jul 2024) governs state-agency AI: bans discriminatory classification, warrantless public biometric surveillance, and deceptive deepfakes; requires human review of irreversible decisions and disclosure of unreviewed GenAI and of AI interactions. Government-use only; no PRA.

citation_bill: RSA 507-H (NH Privacy Act / Expectation of Privacy)
short_title: NH Privacy Act — profiling opt-out
operative_date: 2025-01-01 (assessments apply to processing created/generated after 2024-07-01; not retroactive — 507-H:8 VI)
who_regulated: Persons that conduct business in NH or produce products/services targeted to NH residents meeting volume/revenue thresholds
hook: Consumer opt-out of profiling in furtherance of solely automated decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects (including insurance as a listed effect). Sensitive data includes biometric data processed to uniquely identify. Assessments for high-risk profiling. AG exclusive; express no PRA.
carve_outs: State/local government; nonprofit; IHE; registered national securities association; GLBA financial institution or data; HIPAA CE/BA. Extensive information exemptions (HIPAA, FCRA, DPPA, FERPA, employment context, etc.).
enforcer: Attorney General exclusive (507-H:11 I); enforced as RSA 358-A:2
private_suit: none — Nothing in this chapter shall be construed as providing the basis for, or be subject to, a private right of action for violations under this chapter or any other law (507-H:11 IV)
statutory_damages: none for consumers; UDAP 358-A public enforcement (dollar table not restated here)
cure_period: AG shall give 60-day cure 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31; after 2026-01-01 cure is discretionary using listed factors
nexus: conducts business in this state or produces products or services targeted to residents of this state (507-H:2)
out_of_state_actor: yes if products/services targeted to NH residents and thresholds met
insurance_situs: n/a — legal-effect category includes insurance; GLBA FI/data entity-out. Not insurance-code UR.
thresholds: in a one-year period: at least 35,000 unique consumers (excluding payment-only processing) or at least 10,000 unique consumers and more than 25 percent gross revenue from sale of personal data
retroactivity: assessments not retroactive; apply to processing created or generated after 2024-07-01
safe_harbor: cure; comparable other-law assessments (507-H:8 V); COPPA parental consent compliance
federal_preemption: Airline Deregulation Act information carve; other federal information exemptions
ai_definition: Profiling: any form of automated processing of personal data to evaluate, analyze, or predict personal aspects. Legal/similarly significant effects include provision or denial of financial/lending, housing, insurance, education, criminal justice, employment, health care, or essential goods/services. Biometric data defined (automatic measurements used to identify; photos/audio/video out unless generated to identify).
impact_assessment_discoverable: AG may require disclosure of relevant assessments; confidential and RSA 91-A exempt; privilege not waived (507-H:8 III)
record_retention: silent (assessments must be conducted and documented)
summary: RSA 507-H (in force 1 Jan 2025) is NH comprehensive privacy act with a solely-automated profiling opt-out that lists insurance among legal effects, plus high-risk profiling assessments. AG-only; express no PRA; 60-day cure through 2025 then discretionary. GLBA FI/data out. Thresholds 35k consumers or 10k+25% sale revenue. Not a BIPA and not insurance-code UR.

short_title: Solicitation of children through responsive generative AI communication
who_regulated: Owner/operator of a computer online, Internet, or bulletin-board service, including an AI chat program, LLM bot, chatbot, character AI, or other application whose sole purpose is responsive open-ended generative communication through AI
hook: Liable if, when directing a communication to a child, the operator knows it is made with intent to facilitate/encourage/offer/solicit/recommend that the child imminently engage in sexually explicit conduct, production of such visual depictions, illegal drugs/alcohol, self-harm/suicide, or a crime of violence. AG sole right of action after 90-day cure; liquidated $1,000/violation for the child.
carve_outs: Cloud/telecom/information-service providers for content created/supplied by another; AI chat integral or incidental to a video game, TV, streaming, movie, or similar interactive experience
enforcer: Attorney General sole right of action (507:8-k II)
private_suit: none — AG sole right of action, though damages run to the child/parent/next friend
statutory_damages: not less than liquidated damages of $1,000 per violation (plus proximate damages) — recovered via AG action
cure_period: 90 days after AG written notice of each alleged violation; if assurances satisfactory to AG, AG shall not sue
nexus: silent beyond directing communication to a child (confirm child definition in 639:3)
thresholds: service whose sole purpose is responsive open-ended generative AI communication
criminal_overlay: also crime — ch. 270 also expands RSA 639:3 child-endangerment (crime text not fully isolated this pass)
ai_definition: covers AI chat program, large language model bot, chatbot, character AI, or other computer application whose sole purpose is responsive open-ended generative communication through AI — no separate AI sentence in 507:8-k I
summary: 2025 ch. 270 (signed 1 Aug 2025; 1 Jan 2026) lets the AG (sole plaintiff, 90-day cure) sue generative-AI chat operators that knowingly direct a child toward sex, drugs, self-harm, or violence. Floor $1,000/violation conceptually for the child. Entertainment-integral and conduit carves. Companion 639:3 crime expansion not fully isolated.
